I have the K97 White, Cherry MX switches, essentially the same board without multicolor leds. The switches are smooth, not terribly loud or clicky, the keys are a tad small having transitioned from a keyboard with larger keys. Overall typing is very pleasant. It comes with three fully programmable light schemes (which will obviously be much more on the K95 with the additional colors) allowing you to program any group the way you want it to, as well as a fourth option of all on. It has three brightness settings; bright, too bright, and you looked into the sun so your retina have now been scorched into a fused mass of useless tissue good luck seeing now gimpy oh god why does it hurt. It also has a windows key lock button, and volume controls (which don't actually work in all games oddly enough). This particular board of mine came with the 18 programmable function keys (full sized, also light up) off to the left side which are nice but can be a pain to get working, one you do though they're a nice addition.

The first K97 I received had some issues with the leds burning out (refurb and random keys went out in a week), however I have had this second board for about 2 months now without a single issue. Build quality is nice, metal face plate on the main keyboard section, but plastic face plate on the additional function keys side (all of it is hefty and rigid though). Palm rest is adequate and not unpleasant, just nothing fantastic. My biggest problem (apart from the fear over led failure) is the USB cable, which is extraordinarily thick, coming wrapped in that nylon wire cover stuff you typically see on PSU connectors. It makes the cable inflexible as hell and somewhat problematic for positioning other wires.

Apart from that it's a decent buy assuming you don't get stuck sending boards back for dead LEDs constantly. I managed to pick my K97 up for 90 bucks on a special from Newegg which is no longer running.
